challenges.title: TGA Driving Hours, Rest Times and the Summer Midday Ban

items.title: Driving Hours under TGA
items.text: A maximum of 9 hours of driving time per day (exceptionally 10 hours, no more than twice a week), 56 hours per week, and a maximum of 90 hours per two weeks (ساعات القيادة) — hard to guarantee by hand across many drivers and routes.

items.title: Breaks & Rest Times
items.text: After at most 4.5 hours of continuous driving, a break of at least 45 minutes is mandatory, plus 11 hours of daily rest and 48 hours of rest after a work week. Fine for violations: SAR 2,000 to 5,000.

items.title: Summer Midday Ban at Ramps & Loading Zones
items.text: From June 15 to September 15, loading and unloading at uncovered ramps and loading zones is banned daily between 12:00 and 15:00 — loading times must be scheduled accordingly.

solutions.title: How Klacks Takes the Load Off Logistics in Saudi Arabia
solutions.subtitle: From optimised routes to the summer midday ban — it all fits together.

items.title: Routes Optimised Automatically
items.text: Klacks sequences stops in the most sensible order — short distances, time windows kept, fewer empty runs.

items.title: Working-Time Limits Checked
items.text: The 9-, 56- and 90-hour values can be configured as maximum working time per day, week and two weeks and are monitored in real time — Klacks checks working time, not driving time, and warns before any limit is exceeded. On request, Klacks hard-blocks a breach in automatic planning; with manual planning it stays at a warning.

items.title: Rest Times Checked, Breaks as Blocks
items.text: Klacks checks the 11-hour daily rest and the 48-hour weekly rest you configure; the 45-minute break after 4.5 hours of driving can be scheduled as a block in the route, but is not checked against the break requirement.

items.title: Summer Midday Ban at Ramps as a Blocked Period
items.text: If the window from 12:00 to 15:00 (June 15 to September 15) is stored as a blocked period, Klacks flags assignments within it, and on request automatic planning does not place any loading or unloading at uncovered ramps there.

items.title: Matching License Classes
items.text: Klacks assigns routes only to drivers with the appropriate license — and warns before certifications expire. If a required certification is missing or has expired, Klacks refuses the assignment, in manual planning too — only drivers with a valid certification are scheduled.

items.title: Klacksy Understands Your Request
items.text: "Plan tomorrow’s routes, driver is sick" is enough — Klacksy starts the replanning, and the planning engine takes the configured working and rest time limits and the summer midday ban, configured as a restricted time window, into account.

example.title: Rest Times and the Summer Midday Ban, One Plan
example.text: Klacks checks the configured working and rest time limits and immediately flags assignments within the summer midday ban stored as a blocked period (12:00 to 15:00, June 15 to September 15), so that loading times at uncovered ramps fall outside the window.
